question: A 65-year-old diabetic man is admitted to the general ward with CAP. His CURB-65 score is 3 (confusion, urea 9 mmol/L, RR 26/min). He has no recent hospitalisation. Which empirical antibiotic regimen is most appropriate?

answers.text: Oral amoxicillin 500 mg three times daily alone

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Oral amoxicillin monotherapy is for low-severity outpatient CAP (CURB-65 0–1); CURB-65 3 indicates moderate-to-severe disease requiring hospitalisation and IV therapy with atypical cover.

Correct. CURB-65 ≥3 (moderate-severe CAP) warrants IV beta-lactam cover (co-amoxiclav or ampicillin-sulbactam) combined with a macrolide to cover atypical pathogens — this dual-coverage approach reduces mortality compared to monotherapy.
Pip-tazo + vancomycin is the regimen for severe HAP/VAP with MRSA risk, not community-acquired pneumonia in a previously well patient; this constitutes escalation beyond what is warranted.
Doxycycline monotherapy covers atypical organisms but provides inadequate cover for moderate-severe CAP (CURB-65 3); this severity requires IV therapy and dual-agent regimens.

overallFeedback.feedback: Use CURB-65 to guide antibiotic intensity: 0–1 = oral amoxicillin (outpatient); 2 = consider hospitalisation; 3–5 = IV beta-lactam + macrolide for CAP. MRSA/Pseudomonas cover (pip-tazo/vancomycin) is reserved for HAP/VAP or specific risk factors, not standard CAP.

Excellent. For moderate-severe CAP (CURB-65 ≥3): IV beta-lactam (co-amoxiclav, ampicillin-sulbactam, or cefuroxime) PLUS macrolide (azithromycin or clarithromycin). Atypical cover is mandatory at this severity because Legionella and Mycoplasma carry higher mortality if missed.
